supersedes_for_new_decisions: config/lane_stock_acceptance_bounds.json (round 1, spent: passed its bounds; its held-out seeds are development data from here on)
why_a_new_round: round 1 found two hazards outside its bounds (partial blinding that leaves coverage high can hide the rear product's top and give a wrong class, count and misplaced flag; an empty lane read as one product at 0.5 % range noise, and every lane a cannot-tell at 1 % because the survey producer's floor margin is fixed). The estimator and the depth measurement were changed on development data only; this round measures the changed code once on seeds nobody has read.
decision_unit: one lane survey frame, scored on the lane it was taken for

held_out_population.rule: held_out_generations.fresh of config/perception_splits.json, ascending, the second, fourth... seed (75 of 150; benchmark_perception stock-seeds --round 2); round 1 read the first, third... ones, which with the 6 burned version-1 seeds and the train and validation seeds are now development data
held_out_population.development_data: train and validation seeds (40 recorded) and the round 1 held-out seeds (75 recorded): 690 lanes on which the changes below were chosen

noise_model.description: synthetic perturbation of the recorded depth frame, stock/benchmark.py perturb_depth: every pixel's range is multiplied by (1 + e), e Gaussian with standard deviation equal to the arm's fraction (0.5 %, 1 %, 2 % of range), then 2 % of pixels are dropped to no-return; seeded by SHA-256 of the frame id; the simulator's depth camera is ideal, so this is not a sensor model and says nothing about a real camera's error structure (no flying pixels, no range-dependent bias, no temporal correlation)

arms.oracle: ablation: perfect identity for whatever face is framed
arms.abstain+degrade: stock/benchmark.py degrade_mask: half the frames lose a band of 30-70 % of the depth image rows
arms.noise0.005 / noise0.01 / noise0.02: abstain with the noise model above and 2 % dropout
arms.not_run: channel and channel_embedding arms: the identity channel, registry and calibration are unchanged since round 1 and nothing in this round touches identity

pass_rule: a 'min' bound passes only if the LOWER limit of the 95 % Wilson interval is at or above the value, a 'max' bound only if the UPPER limit is at or below it, and only with required_n met; otherwise fail (point estimate on the wrong side) or inconclusive. 'answered_wrong' counts answered lanes more than one product off, and any product read in a lane that is empty (so a phantom is wrong even though it is within one). One run per arm; no re-tuning.

refusals_added: top surface supports a number of products that disagrees with the depth count by more than 1.2 (was: widen the range)
nearest surface supported by fewer bins than 0.7 of the smallest pitch
a step in the top height shorter than that
no class claim when the frame's bed sigma exceeds max_sigma_for_class_m
